A1.justification: Both complete 11-page PDFs describe the same CODA work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet reconstruction and generation experiments in Tables 2–3, supported by ablations and visual analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds MS-COCO text-to-image generation results in Table 5.

M1.justification: The documented residual quantization, attention-based assignment, LoRA adaptation, losses and MaskGIT procedures are unchanged. The new text-to-image evaluation introduces no described method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds MS-COCO text-to-image evaluation in Table 5. This substantially broadens the previously ImageNet-only coverage through both a new dataset and a distinct text-conditioned generation task.

E2.justification: New Table 5 introduces VQ-Diffusion and U-Net as reported comparators, alongside U-ViT-S. The comparator sets in the retained ImageNet experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 5 introduces evaluations using CODA MaskGIT-S and U-ViT-S configurations. Existing ImageNet training budgets, metrics and sampling settings remain unchanged; MS-COCO-specific splits, training budgets and sampling settings are not documented.

E4.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the same component, LoRA, codebook-size and normalization ablations. Figures 3–6 retain the same latent-space, residual-level, assignment and training-dynamics analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added Table 5 follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds FIDs of 13.86, 7.32, 5.95 and 5.44 for VQ-Diffusion, U-Net, U-ViT-S and CODA MaskGIT-S, respectively. Existing results are retained; SSIM rescaling and Table 4c's PSNR precision change from 21.5 to 21.51 do not establish changed performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Sections 3–4, including the residual and attention quantization formulations and training losses, are unchanged. No new assumptions, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about decoupling compression from discretization, reconstruction quality, full codebook utilization and reduced training budget. The additional benchmark does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning representational capacity, sparse assignment, codebook utilization and the asymmetric benefits of decoder versus encoder adaptation remain unchanged. No substantive new limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Implementation details, LoRA rank, quantization levels, learning rates, batch sizes, training durations and the project link are unchanged. The added MS-COCO experiment receives no accompanying implementation or reproducibility details.

R1.justification: v2 adds AdaNAT as reference 30 and cites it in the introduction's discussion of efficient discrete generation. The existing literature coverage and research positioning otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses explanations in Section 2.1, corrects several typographical errors and adds acknowledgements. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, adjusts figure sizing and typography, and reflows surrounding text. Tables 1, 2 and 4 display SSIM as decimals rather than percentage-style values; existing figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Table 5 provides limited evidence of applicability beyond v1's ImageNet-only experiments by adding MS-COCO text-to-image evaluation. Clearer SSIM notation and proofreading also help. However, missing protocol and implementation details for the new experiment limit its reproducibility and the strength of the added evidence.
